finding: adopt() keeps a `record` parameter its body no longer reads
why: The delta moved the merge into owner.append_owner, which re-reads the file, so the in-memory record the caller passes at line 434 is dead input.
fix: Drop the `record` parameter from adopt() and its call site (and the test calls) or note why it stays.
evidence: def adopt(owner, record_file: Path, record: dict) -> None: ... owner.append_owner(str(record_file), mine, primary=True)  (the removed lines were the only readers: `record.update(...)`, `owner.owners_of(record)`, `record["owners"] = ...`)

finding: Possible fragile closure: `real` is rebound from Path.write_text to os.replace while the earlier write_text stub still calls `real(self, ...)`.
why: The stub at line 462-463 reads `real` at call time, so any later Path.write_text on a file other than record_file would call os.replace and fail in a confusing way.
fix: Name the second saved function differently, for example `real_replace`.
evidence: line 461 `real = Path.write_text`; line 463 `... else real(self, *a, **k))`; added line 466 `real, refusals = os.replace, []`

finding: Possible gap: the case-insensitive `-sup` check in `_check_agent_id` has no test with a mixed-case id.
why: The change claims all three checks fold case, but only `Contact` and the `A1` twin are tested, so dropping `.lower()` from the `endswith("-sup")` check would pass every test.
fix: Add the pair ("X-SUP", "ends in -sup") to the parametrize list.

finding: Possible weak bound: the give-up half of the patient test only asserts `len(calls) > 3`.
why: A change that cuts the retry loop from 100 tries to 3 still passes both halves, so the 2 s patience the docstring promises is not pinned.
fix: Assert the exact attempt count (101) or a lower bound near the loop size.
evidence: scripts/worktree_owner.py:272 `for _ in range(100):`; test line `assert len(calls) > 3`

finding: The parametrized append_owner test steers its asserts with try/except and an `added` flag.
why: One body covers two behaviours (retry succeeds, retry gives up), which hides which one a failure belongs to.
fix: Split into two tests, or use `pytest.raises` in the give-up case.
evidence: `try: owner.append_owner(...) except PermissionError: assert not added`
